body:
Fixes #333.

Indented Q&A consumers currently reconstruct children from the private
`_isFromPathCombination` flag and maintain their own escaping and array-versus-text
heuristics. This adds public JavaScript APIs for reading and writing those
documents directly:

- `Parser.parseGroups()` returns `LinksGroup` objects with each line's `element`
  and immediate `children`, including deeper indentation and named links.
- `escapeReference(text, { minimal: true })` leaves ordinary prose spaces bare
  and doubles enclosing quotes when quoting is needed. It protects structural
  characters, significant whitespace, comment starts, and reserved literal
  prefixes anywhere in the line.
- `unescapeReference()` and `Link.unescapeReference()` decode complete quoted
  references and versioned literals. Parsed Link IDs are already decoded.
- `parseIndentedDocument()` and `formatIndentedDocument()` convert between
  indented text and `Map<string, string | string[]>`, with two-space child
  indentation and a trailing newline. Multiple children default to an array;
  `{ multipleValues: 'join' }` explicitly combines them as multiline text.

For example:

```js
const answers = parseIndentedDocument(
  'What is your experience?\n  I have worked with JavaScript\n'
);
answers.get('What is your experience?'); // 'I have worked with JavaScript'
formatIndentedDocument(answers); // Same plain text with two-space indentation
```

The scope is the JavaScript package used by the issue's linked consumer. The
document helpers reject grandchildren and named links with values; use
`parseGroups()` for those structures. One-element arrays read back as strings
because the syntax cannot distinguish them. Empty arrays and empty strings
remain distinct; duplicate parents accumulate children in order.

The latest main branch is merged, including #335's lossless reference literals.
Default Link formatting continues to use its shared canonical encoder. Empty
strings and controls, including exact multiline line endings, use those literals
in minimal mode as well. Release metadata, installation snippets and the
generated benchmark report are prepared for 0.25.0 across all seven
implementations to satisfy the mandatory version-consistency check.

English/Russian documentation, TypeScript declarations, a runnable
[Q&A example](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/blob/issue-333-056bb2173c3b/examples/js_indented_document.js),
and a CI declaration check are included. The
[investigation notes](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/blob/issue-333-056bb2173c3b/experiments/issue-333/README.md)
record the reproducing tests and CI fixes.

Validation:

- Before implementation, the new JavaScript test file reported 10 failures.
  Afterward, all 307 JavaScript tests pass. Reproduce and verify with
  `cd js && bun test tests/IndentedDocument.test.js`. Its 14 tests cover the
  issue example, grouping, multiple-value policies, doubled quotes, exact
  whitespace, Unicode, empty values, parser limits and invalid structures.
- Integration regressions first failed on reserved literal-looking text and
  literal decoding. They now verify the shared 91-reference corpus and reserved
  prefixes both at the start and in the middle of prose, including the case
  where `text ~1{61} after` previously became `text a after`.
- The finite [round-trip probe](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/blob/issue-333-056bb2173c3b/experiments/issue-333/reference-roundtrip.mjs)
  verifies 2,380 short strings through serialized references, ordinary parsing
  and document Maps against both source and built package.
- Local Python, Rust, C#, Go (with race detection), PHP and Java suites pass.
  JavaScript build, lint, formatting, TypeScript checks, both runnable examples,
  dependency freshness, npm/Bun locks, release consistency, documentation
  checks/build and Java/PHP formatting checks pass.
- All seven bindings produce identical bytes and decoded text for 1,392 binary
  interoperability cases. The benchmark generator verifies all 73 generated
  files without drift.

CI passes on `bc035a5`: all 17 active workflows completed successfully,
including all seven language suites, security, binary interoperability,
benchmarks, dependency freshness and the C# PDF artifact job.
